verdicts.note: Tested toward 0. He reports no elected experience [S1] and is challenging the incumbent. He pitches himself as 'a hands-on problem solver' who offers 'practical solutions' [S1] and does not make an explicit call for new voices. +1 at medium is right. No spending score is missing: 'responsible, transparent budgeting for taxpayers' comes paired with commitments to support jobs, small businesses, roads and critical infrastructure [S1]. That cuts both ways, so it does not support a restraint lean.

Tested toward -2. He is a one-term incumbent (3.5 years, won 1,632 to 1,571 in 2022 [S3]) running explicitly to 'continue the progress made' [S1]. One term keeps it at -1. High confidence is acceptable because both incumbency and the continuity framing are explicit facts from a tier-1 statement and results [S1][S3].

Tested toward 0 and toward low confidence. His statement keeps returning to restraint: 'the importance of every taxpayer dollar', 'fiscal responsibility', a treasury 'managed with integrity and transparency', and 'government efficiency that respects ... your tax dollars' [S1]. That is the audit-and-restrain pole in general terms, with no specific cuts, so -1 and not -2. I checked whether his EMS District No. 1 record points the other way: seconding an exempt director salary and approving a $52,000 transfer to a building fund [S2]. These are routine special-district actions, not an expansionary agenda, and they do not undercut the score. Medium fits.
